pages.text: News Detail Share Close Agrifood economics and policy Satellite-based maize forecasts show promising results in Zimbabwe 05/11/2026 Harare, Zimbabwe, 28 October 2026 – Technical experts from national and regional institutions gathered in Harare on 27 and 28 October for a two-day hands-on workshop to explore the potential of satellite-based technologies to improve maize area and yield forecasting in Zimbabwe. Organized by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) office in Zimbabwe under the Earth Observations for Crop Data (ESTELLA) programme, the workshop introduced participants to the Agriculture Remotely-sensed Yield Algorithm (ARYA). Developed by the University of Valencia , ARYA is being tested under ESTELLA to strengthen agricultural data and statistics through Earth Observation (EO) technologies. The workshop brought together 17 participants from eight national and regional institutions, as well as FAO staff. Participants explored the entire ARYA forecasting process, from satellite data preparation to generating maize planted area and yield estimates. pages.text: News details | FAO in Cambodia | Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Share Close Cambodia Unlocking New Opportunities for Cambodia's Mango Sector 27/07/2026 , Cambodia Growing high-quality mangoes is important, but farmers can earn more when they have access to processing, reliable buyers, and markets that value their products. Understanding what investors, processors, and consumers need is an important step toward creating more opportunities for farming communities. As Cambodia diversifies its agrifood systems beyond rice, mango has emerged as one of the country's most promising agricultural products. Between 2016 and 2020, the area under mango cultivation expanded from around 5,000 hectares to approximately 138,000 hectares, with production reaching an estimated 1.5 million tonnes. Today, mango is Cambodia's priority product under FAO's One Country One Priority Product (OCOP) initiative, reflecting its strong economic potential and cultural significance. Located on the ground floor, the pressroom is supported by the Public Information Office, which is dedicated to facilitating accurate coverage of the Court and furthering the public’s understanding of the Court’s function and history. The main office number is 202-479-3211. Recorded information—such as the opinion and orders forecast for the coming week or the list of opinions released that day—is available on this line, and reporters may also reach a staff member by pressing 1. The office is open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. A number of materials of interest to news media are available on the Court’s website: orders , opinions , calendars , oral argument transcripts and audio , as well as information about obtaining case updates and briefs . The publication, One Country One Priority Product at Five - Celebrating the Impact. Growing the Future ., reveals the results achieved by the 94 FAO Members who have joined the FAO-led initiative since it started in September 2021. Governments, farmers, producers’ organizations, value chain actors, research institutions, development partners and private-sector stakeholders are working together to strengthen the value chains of 56 special agricultural products (SAPs). “ This publication reflects the commitment, expertise and dedication of many individuals and insitutions across the OCOP initiative ,” writes Yurdi Yasmi , Executive Secretary of the OCOP Secretariat and Director of the FAO Plant Production and Protection Division, noting that the country-led, country-owned initiative and demand-driven initiative has become “a global movement”. The High-Level Event, held as part of the World Food Forum 2026, reviewed progress made since the initiative was launched in 2021 and explored opportunities to scale successful models and accelerate impact for farmers, rural communities and agrifood systems worldwide. Opening the event, FAO Director-General QU Dongyu highlighted the initiative’s role in helping countries design a holistic way to promote a national brand through a special agricultural product. “ Behind each product are farmers, communities, knowledge, businesses and markets. Also, we start with a country’s own strengths and comparative advantages ,” he said. “ OCOP is showing tangible results ,” he emphasized, explaining that priority products can become the entry point for wider transformation – raising farmers’ incomes, creating rural jobs, attracting investments and building resilience. Newly installed GIES environmental monitoring station in Gazipur, Bangladesh. ©FAO/Naila Fahmin Rasha 18/11/2026 Dhaka, Bangladesh – Bangladesh has taken an important step towards building a stronger scientific identity for its jackfruit through Geographical Indications Environment & Sustainability (GIES), a science-based approach that connects agricultural products with reliable information about their geographical origin, growing environment and product characteristics. As part of this effort, a GIES environmental monitoring station has been installed in a jackfruit-growing area in Gazipur. The station will support systematic environmental monitoring and scientific documentation of the production area. The work is being carried out under the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) One Country One Priority Product (OCOP) initiative, supported by the Government of the People’s Republic of China through the FAO–China South-South Cooperation Programme. Countries participating in FAO’s One Country One Priority Product (OCOP) initiative showcased their unique agricultural products through vibrant displays, tastings and storytelling. Visitors discovered the people, knowledge, traditions and biodiversity behind the products, as well as their potential to strengthen value chains, improve livelihoods and reach new markets. The meeting set out the strategic direction, governance framework, and operational priorities needed to move the project into full-scale implementation. The initiative supports 15 demonstration countries across all regions in developing sustainable value chains for Special Agricultural Products—selected for their economic value, cultural significance, and potential to drive agrifood systems transformation. With support from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), 75 farmers and producers, processors, exporters and regional agricultural officials took part in practical training addressing challenges across the value chain. The programme connected climate-resilient orchard management with water efficiency, plant health, post-harvest management, food safety and market requirements. The side event which took place on 20 October 2026 showcased progress in the application of FAO's Tool for Agroecology Performance Evaluation (TAPE), which is being used worldwide to assess the multidimensional (economic, social, environmental, health and nutrition and governance) performance of agroecology. It also examined how TAPE can connect farm-level assessments with research, national monitoring, and policy dialogue. United States Department of Transportation In This Section Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen) The Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen) was a large-scale FAA initiative to modernize the U.S. National Airspace System (NAS). Through NextGen, the FAA revamped air traffic control infrastructure for communications, navigation, surveillance, automation, and information management to increase the safety, efficiency, capacity, predictability, flexibility, and resiliency of U.S. aviation. NextGen’s scope included airport infrastructure improvements, new air traffic technologies and procedures, and safety and security enhancements. We engaged with the public and shared practices with the aviation community to accelerate the adoption of innovative technologies. Our modernization initiative enabled a more flexible — yet robust and resilient — aerospace infrastructure that ensures the safe introduction of non-traditional aviation, such as commercial space transportation and advanced air mobility. This allows quality values to be tightly defined and then numerically calibrated, which in turn allows for the standardization needed to support a worldwide deployment of fingerprint sensors with universally interpretable image qualities. NFIQ 2 quality features are formally standardized as part of ISO/IEC 29794-4 and serve as the reference implementation of the standard. Most, but not all of them, have improved their chances Doug Farrar Wed 11 Nov 2026 04.00 EST Last modified on Wed 11 Nov 2026 10.30 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Vikings get the QB they desperately need After what happened Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings had to do this. In a dispiriting loss to the Buffalo Bills, the Vikings saw their tremendous defense go to waste, as Carson Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions and a passer rating of 8.9. It was one of the worst quarterback performances in recent history , and it continued a run of recent QB futility for the Vikings, from JJ McCarthy to Kyler Murray to Wentz. pages.text: NG Stories | Past exhibitions | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Past exhibition NG Stories: Making a National Gallery 4 October 2024 - 12 January 2025 Admission free Gallery B Immerse yourself in 200 years of extraordinary National Gallery stories. From a resident family of 14 and an intrepid travelling agent to ground-breaking scientists and a wartime pianist, NG Stories tells the history of the National Gallery through the people who made us what we are today. There’s a slate mine in Wales where paintings were safely stored during the Second World War. A guard dog who became a member of staff. And a Keeper’s family, with 14 children, who lived in the building and kept diaries. You’ll discover some of the untold personal stories of the Gallery and the special memories we have been privileged to help create for our visitors. From childhood adventures to life-changing first art encounters, our visitors have always been at the heart of what we do. Through magical soundscapes and immersive digital interactions, you'll experience the work of the many people here at the Gallery who help to care for the paintings and see how this work has changed over the years.
